subject: Safeguard clause: court access vs arbitration trigger
messages:
From: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@novusretail.com>
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Mark Reyes <mark.reyes@novusretail.com>
Date: 2027-11-02T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: MSA redlines + emergency relief carveout

Karthik / Lauren —

Thanks for sending the draft MSA. Attached are Novus Retail's initial redlines (Novus_MSA_redline_v3.docx) and a short note from our GC. High level concerns we want to surface up front:

- We support arbitration for most disputes, but we need clear, immediate access to courts for injunctive or emergency relief where there is a risk of IP or customer data exfiltration.
- We'd prefer New York (state) as governing law and a New York court for any emergency filings.
- We want a short carveout that allows interim injunctive relief in court without waiving the right to arbitrate the underlying dispute.
- Also flagged obligations around preservation and expedited discovery in the event of emergency relief — see Keller & Associates' note attached.

Can you confirm Redwood's position on: whether emergency court access can be mutual and narrowly tailored, and whether you can accept New York as a potential forum for urgent relief?

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call.

— Olivia
General Counsel, Novus Retail
Attachments: Novus_MSA_redline_v3.docx (docx), Keller_comments.pdf (pdf)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@novusretail.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-02T11:18:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines + emergency relief carveout

Olivia —

Appreciate the clear note and the redlines. Looping in Monica from legal ops to help coordinate. Quick summary of Redwood's initial posture:

- We agree arbitration should be the primary forum for final resolution, but we have to preserve the ability to seek urgent, narrowly-tailored interim relief in court (to protect both parties).
- Redwood is uncomfortable with an unconditional forum selection to a single state for all emergency filings — that creates latency risk for customers and for Redwood in cross-border situations.
- Proposal idea (high-level): allow emergency injunctive relief to be sought in any court with competent jurisdiction where the claimant demonstrates imminent irreparable harm or risk of data loss, provided Redwood gets prompt notice and an agreement to stay any final remedies to arbitration.
- We can be flexible on governing law as part of negotiation; if Novus strongly prefers New York for emergency filings we could accept a split approach: governing law = California, with emergency forum carveouts that include New York where Novus has significant operations.

Practical ask: could Keller send a short redline that limits court relief to "preliminary injunctive or conservatory measures only" and adds a mutuality requirement? That would make it easier for legal to accept.

Happy to discuss live tomorrow.

Thanks,
Karthik
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Keller & Associates (gc@kellerlaw.com)
To: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@novusretail.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-03T10:45:00-05:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines + emergency relief carveout

Karthik / Olivia —

Attached are our suggested edits (Keller_comments.pdf) and an alternate redline. Key points from counsel perspective:

- We can live with arbitration as default, but the carveout must expressly permit either party to seek interim equitable relief (injunctive, provisional remedies) in a state or federal court of competent jurisdiction without being deemed to have waived arbitration.
- "Interim" should be defined and limited: court relief may be sought only to preserve status quo or prevent imminent loss; the parties must proceed to arbitration for the merits.
- We ask for a short, mutual notice period (48 hours) unless circumstances make notice impossible — include language requiring "reasonable efforts to provide notice".
- We are asking for explicit language about expedited preservation/discovery limited to materials directly relevant to the emergency relief; Redwood should be spared broad discovery before arbitrator appointment.
- On choice of law/venue: Novus prefers New York for emergency filings but proposes that emergency filings may be brought "in any court where a party maintains assets or a principal place of business" — that gives some flexibility.

If Redwood can accept the "interim only" limitation, mutual notice requirement, and a tight preservation/discovery scope, Novus is willing to move quickly. See attached suggested clause: "Emergency Relief; Arbitration to Proceed".

— Keller (on behalf of Novus Retail)
Attachments: Keller_comments.pdf (pdf)

From: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Olivia Grant <olivia.grant@novusretail.com>, Keller & Associates (gc@kellerlaw.com)
Cc: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, monica_patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-04T16:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: MSA redlines + emergency relief carveout

Olivia / Keller —

Thanks for the thoughtful redlines and suggested language. Redwood Legal has reviewed and we think there is a reasonable compromise that addresses Novus' concerns while protecting Redwood's operational requirements. Summary of Redwood's proposed clause (attached: Redwood_emergency-carveout-proposal.docx):

- Emergency relief carveout: Either party may seek preliminary or provisional injunctive relief in a court of competent jurisdiction to prevent imminent and irreparable harm, including in cases of suspected data exfiltration or clear IP misappropriation.
- Scope: Limited to interim relief (to preserve status quo) — final remedies and the ultimate dispute remain subject to binding arbitration under the agreement.
- Venue: Emergency filings may be brought in (i) a court where the claimant has assets or a principal place of business, or (ii) in California federal or state court if Redwood is the claimant. We are amenable to New York being an acceptable option for Novus where Novus has significant operations.
- Notice & discovery: The party seeking emergency relief must make reasonable efforts to provide notice; if notice is impossible due to urgency, the right remains. Preservation obligations are required, but any expedited discovery will be narrowly tailored and limited to materials necessary to adjudicate the emergency relief.
- Mutuality: The clause is mutual and non-waiving (seeking emergency relief does not waive right to arbitration).

Next steps: If this core language is acceptable in principle, can Keller produce a tracked redline replacing Novus' current carveout with the attached proposal? We'd like to finalize language this week to keep DEAL-9932 on schedule.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Director, Legal Operations — Redwood Inference
Attachments: Redwood_emergency-carveout-proposal.docx (docx)
